newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open up, electronic shares active.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open up, electronic shares active.

text.p: The Singapore stock market was a tad firmer at mid-morning on Thursday with renewed interest in electronic counters, dealers said.
At 0230 GMT, the key Straits Times Industrials Index was up 7.05 points at 2,053.50. Turnover was around 47 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 108 to 81.

"All the top actives are electronic counters," a dealer said. "This sector has been re-rated. Analysts believe the cycle is near the bottom and a recovery is expected in the first quarter due to improved U.S. book-to-bill ratio."
Expectations were for even better October data after the September U.S. semiconductor book-to-bill rose to 0.99 from 0.93 in August.
Leading the actives at mid-morning were electronic counters Uraco holdings, SMB United, Advanced Systems Automation and Sunright Ltd, all with at least two million shares traded.
Foreign counters of SIA, Singapore Press and OCBC led the gainers, rising S$0.20-0.30 (US$0.14-0.21), albeit in light volumes.
Malaysian over the counter stocks Tasek Cement and Renong Bhd shed S$0.20 and S$0.07 to S$3.90 and S$2.30 respectively.
